utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness Y.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: There is a technical problem. There is a technical problem. Two booths cannot hear the floor, the English and the B/C/S booth cannot hear anything from the floor. The B/C/S booth can now, but the English booth cannot hear anything. Could counsel say something now? I think it's sorted out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Good afternoon, Witness Y.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There has been a slight delay because of a technical problem, but I think we can now proceed. At this time, I would ask the usher to display the next Prosecution Exhibit which is identical to the exhibit that has already been tendered by the Defence yesterday, D9-2. We don't have copies for anyone because it's exactly the same as was tendered yesterday, so there's no difference, and the only reason we're using this instead of the Defence Exhibit is because we are going to do a little marking on it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So this map will then be marked Prosecution Exhibit 227.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness Y, could you look at that exhibit, which is number 227, and tell us generally what that shows.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In principal it shows the deployment of forces, of all three forces, that is; that is to say, the army, the HVO, and the Chetnik forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we have talked throughout this trial about the front in Turbe and the front in Visoko. Could you show us where those two fronts are on that map, perhaps using the pointer which is in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Turbe (indicating), Visoko (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think Defence counsel may have had a hard time seeing that. Is it possible to sit and point at the same time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Turbe (indicating). I think that this is Visoko over here. It doesn't say so on the map, but I think that it's there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, along the fronts, you see red lines and blue lines. Tell us first what those red lines represent.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Chetnik forces. The blue lines are the BH army forces. And over here, there are HVO forces, a little bit, and here too (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So according to this map, there were some HVO forces along the frontline with the Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as you can see, but very few.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the map indicate where the majority of HVO forces were during this time period which is marked on the map December '92 and January '93?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where does this map indicate that the majority of the HVO forces were located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating). The Lasva Valley.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've already told us about the 325th command. Does this map indicate the presence of the 325th command, and if so, can you find it for us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The command of the 325th was located in Kruscica, over here, exactly over here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a symbol there that indicates that this was, in fact, a command rather than a manned battalion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The little triangle here, and what you see up here above. At any rate, this triangle depicts the exact location of the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it says, next to that Kruscica with the triangle, it says 1/325. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That means that the command of the 1st battalion of the 325th brigade was also there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you find the 2nd battalion of the 325th brigade on that map, and tell us where it is, if you find it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Preocica (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that also a command, or was it a manned battalion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only the command of the battalion. I'm sorry. Perhaps -- could I elaborate on it a bit?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It wasn't the entire command that was in these locations, only part of the command of the battalion, because another part of the command of the battalion was with our fighters who were on the frontline at Turbe and in Visoko. As far as manpower is concerned, there were five to seven men, up to a maximum of ten altogether.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you find the village of Loncari on this map and Nadioci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nadioci, Loncari (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see a blue circle next to Loncari?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that blue circle signify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that Ahmici, the village of Ahmici, is somewhere around here, and as a symbol on the map, it doesn't mean a thing to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see other blue circles on that map that are empty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what those empty blue circles signify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see blue circles that are not empty that have symbols in them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do they symbolise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that these abbreviations symbolise how strong the unit was. Over here, we have an abbreviation saying "V" standing for "Vod" which is "platoon."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would that signify to you that stationed in that circle with the "V" would be, in fact, a platoon of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell us about some of the symbols that you see in that map that are, in fact, in the Lasva Valley but that are red?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't see any red signs in the Lasva Valley.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see any symbols for weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you point them out for us and tell us what they symbolise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These two symbols are anti-aircraft guns. This symbol is a launcher. This too. This is also the symbol for a particular piece, but I'm not sure which one (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do these symbols for these weapons indicate to which army these weapons belong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to this map, which army possessed those weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you take the green marker there in front of you and circle for us some of those HVO weapons that are placed on that map in and around the Lasva Valley, and as you do so, tell us what you're circling.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is an anti-aircraft gun (indicating). Likewise. This is a launcher (indicating). The last two I circled were mortars. I think that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you see any symbols for checkpoints in the Lasva Valley?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does the symbol for the checkpoint look like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A circle, and in one circle there is a letter "P" written in black.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What would that letter "P" signify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: ^ "Punkt" which is "checkpoint."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would these be red checkpoints or blue checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Red.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And therefore which side had those checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you circle the checkpoints that you see in the Lasva Valley, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The checkpoint Dubravica, its precise location is the railway station. Checkpoint at Puticevo; that is as you go out of Novi Travnik. There are more of them here, but I only know of these two, and I saw them personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've also mentioned some villages during the course of your testimony. If I read them off, can you find them on the map and underline them for us? Kovacevac, and underline them using your green.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Strane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Rovna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Loncari?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pezici, if you can find it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They're not on the map, but they're somewhere around here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Same general area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, over here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Merdani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think it's here on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be in the same general area as the other villages you've underlined?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that Merdani is somewhere over here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in the same general area as Loncari and Strane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the broader area. Merdani is on the right-hand side of the Lasva River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Jelinak and Putis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Marks). Jelinak, Putis (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You can sit down. Were there any BiH battalions in Ahmici before April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than the command that you've pointed out for the 325th, where were the BiH army battalions located at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were at the front, at Turbe and Visoko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know an area -- I think we've talked about this briefly -- called Kuber?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you underline that so we can find it later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what was at Kuber?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only know that there was a HVO unit at Kuber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just so we can orient ourselves a little bit, looking at that big map of Ahmici which is partly covered by the military map, in what direction would you have to go from Ahmici in order to get to Kuber? Would it be closer to go through the Upper Ahmici area or through the other side of Ahmici, down through Santici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Through Upper Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just a couple of more questions about that map. There are some blue circles up near the Travnik area, and I think you may have mentioned it before. Those blue circles have the letter V in them. Do you see what I'm referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, again, what those blue circles signified and what those troops were doing there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I've already said, the V is an abbreviation for "VOD," which is a platoon. As for the units, as this was quite close to the battlefield, the frontline towards the Serbs, the units were located there if the need arose for them to intervene and maintain a defence towards the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then within the valley you see some blue circles with nothing in them, no V, empty. Were there any BiH troops located in those blue circles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you have any explanation or can you provide any explanation as to what those empty blue circles mean on that map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I have no idea. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: We will, at this time, offer into evidence Exhibits 225, 226 and 227, the first two under seal and the last one not under seal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness will be interrogated by Defence counsel Ranko Radovic and Jadranka Slokovic-Glumac.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I will be brief and my colleague will not be that brief, so we have changed roles as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: By way of introduction, may I ask you for a closed session lest some surnames slip my tongue, because I will have to be asking questions about certain individuals, specific individuals. (Closed session)

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: (Open session)

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, what ways did you pull out towards Vrhovine? How was this retreat organised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In groups. Groups of 10 to 20 women, elderly men, and children.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: How many people managed to get up to Vrhovine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Could it have been around 500 people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how large the groups were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Up to 20 people per group.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did you try to organise it so that these groups would be escorted by soldiers or by a person with a rifle on that person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: How many such soldiers with rifles went up towards Vrhovine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were two per group.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: So there could have been some ten groups in view of the number of people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, where was the line of defence established on the 17th, on your side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The defence line?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it was at Barica Gaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: How many people manned the line at Barica Gaj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Were you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but for a short while.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: How many people were -- during the short while that you were there, how many people were there then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, try to say.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How can I say when I don't know exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you exactly. Was it more than 20 people, more than 50, more than 100?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Up to 20 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: How far is it from Ahmici to Vrhovine on foot? How much time does it take you to get there, for instance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe 30 to 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: This line of defence which was set up in Barica, when was that? Was that already on the 17th, in the morning of the 17th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: This line was held by 20 people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And those are people from the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and there were some people from Vrhovine also.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did any units from Zenica come to your assistance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: You know for a fact that it didn't, or is it possible they came but you don't know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I know for a fact that they didn't, that one didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Does the name Fehim Mujezinovic (phoen) mean anything to you? It doesn't mean anything to you? You don't know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: If I help you and tell you that he was the commanding officer, the commander of the Zenica unit which came to help you on that day, who was killed at Barica Gaj on the first day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Until what time were you at Barica Gaj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We came up in the early hours of the morning and I stayed there for at most two or three hours and then we returned because the people from Vrhovine had come in the meantime to see what had happened to us. I went --

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to Vrhovine.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Why did you go to Vrhovine? To join the staff or what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to Vrhovine, first of all, because my family was there, to see them, to tell them that I was alive, to have a bite to eat and to recuperate a bit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could we have a closed session for a minute only?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. (Closed session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: 25 (Open session) (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Let us continue. The last thing that we were discussing was this information about putting units in the first degree of combat readiness. And you said that as far as you were concerned, that meant taking rifles and shooting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not as far as I was concerned, as far as organised troops and organised army on the lines was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: But this cable was sent directly to you, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall to whom it was sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: To whom could it have been sent if not you, if you were the person in command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not in command at all, I was just the organiser.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but whenever command is referred to in this diary, your name is also there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, tell me who whom else it could have been sent but to you. To only you, to just you, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And your reaction to that cable was what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To reinforce the guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: But you had done that before that. Now, when we talked the previous date, you said that you had reinforced the guards then. You said that a cable had arrived for patrols to be reinforce and for more reconnoitring to be done. How come you did not receive a similar telegram?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Then, I mean. Okay. So your reaction then, was it to just reinforce the guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We were to inspect the guards to see how many people were in the guards, and to see how many reinforcements were needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any people on furlough from the army in the village then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: How many such people were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Can you say how many members of the B and H army were in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between 30 and 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that the total number of the members of the B and H army there was between 30 and 40, and in addition to that there were people engaged in the village guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, elderly people.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any minors in the village guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that there were some.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, in the middle part of the village, in middle Ahmici, how many members of the village guards were there? You said in the lower part of the section there were, if I'm not wrong -- what did you say? I'm sorry, I forgot.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand. Do you mean in one shift?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, not in one shift.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The total.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah, the total number, that's what I mean. How many people have been envisaged to stand guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The envisaged number was two for the guard shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: How many people were on the list of guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that -- you don't know for the lower part of the village either?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, because as I told you, I didn't draw up those lists of people to stand guard. I rather inspected the guards and saw to -- sought to deal with problems and talk to the people and ask them to stand guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: So these guards were organised in pairs, two people, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And they took shifts -- they took turns every two hours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not necessarily every two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly. It depended on the people directly involved. As the need arose, that is the way they organised the shifts.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: So it could have been longer you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It usually was longer, because there were only a few people that could stand guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: So how many people did you need, because you stood guard from the evening till the morning. How many people did it take? How many people did you need?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean during one night?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For one shift up to eight people were needed, for the entire village that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: From say, 8.00 p.m. to 8.00 a.m. The next morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I can't say exactly from what time to what time, but it was in the evening, in the night hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: That would make 24 people if they took turns every two hours per section of the village. The entire village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not the entire village.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: You said in principle they would stand guard for two hours, from the evening till the next morning, so we can take that to be from 8.00 p.m. to 8.00 a.m. The next morning, which is 12 hours, meaning 2 hours, 6 people, meaning 12 people per section of the village per night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How many did you say? What was the total?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Twelve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: So four sections of the village required during one night only, approximately 48 people per night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not that many. There were never that many. It was envisaged, yes, but there were never so many out there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: But these people would not stand guard the next night, of course, the following night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did. As a rule they would go out the next night, because we didn't have enough people and usually they did. And sometimes even a single person would stand guard two shifts per night because of the lack of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: But in view of the number of people in the village, could the number that we could reach as of people having been involved in the guard be a hundred for the whole four sections?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, much less.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: What would you say if I told you, and I've already told you this, that 27 people were on the list for the middle part of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is possible. It is possible. That is to say all the people who lived there were those people. Of course, not all of them stood guard. Some were, for example, on vacation. They were members of the army and they were on vacation. Of course we couldn't make them stand guard too. I don't know who are the people who are on this list, but perhaps there are minors there too and we planned to put them on guard duty because of the insufficient number we had, but I think that's it. So these were the people that he had -- that were made available to him in that part of the village. Whether all of them stood guard or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please look at this table on page 3 so that you would see the pairs that were made. So it wasn't all the people, these are the people who were listed as members of the guard. Those are the people from that list.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. Yes. Yes. These are the people from that part of the village, all the people who were planned for guard duty. However, some of these people had jobs, who were not at home, who were on the frontline against the Serbs. So this was a total list from that part of the village. And, of course, he could never get this many people because there weren't -- they weren't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: According to this list, these were the people who went out for guard duty, and it says so on the 7th of March, that all of these people are duty-bound to stand guard duty, and if they cannot, that they have to find themselves a replacement. And number three says if they do not go out for guard duty, this person would be sent to prison and would not get a certificate showing why they could not appear in their regular jobs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, these were only our wishes. This was wishful thinking. We hoped we could make them go on guard duty this way but we couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Was there actually someplace you could take them to prison, like Preocica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to tell you what it says on the 15th of April, 1993. "Before dark I went to Preocica, I drove my wife. Then I got back home. I learned that the Croats were concentrating around the Kupreskic houses. We held a meeting (the command) at my place at 20.00 hours. We agreed to set up lines in case of trouble, and then how and in what way to act. Nidjro, Sisko and I agreed to met the next day at 14.00 hours by the line in the direction of Gudura. In the warehouse I was issued with 7.62 ammunition, 7.9 ammunition, 45 pieces grenade launchers, 3 pieces made in Zenica explosive devices, two times three cartridges of plastic explosive.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, you said that there was a meeting in that house at 20.00 hours that evening, and you said that you agreed that you would reinforce the guard, and here it says that if some problems cropped up that you would reinforce the line, how to function, in what way. Is this here true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: So you didn't talk about doubling the guard, you had done that earlier already, but now you agreed on what should be done if something happened in the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, again, we reviewed the guard. There were always, always problems with the guard, constantly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to agreeing on the line in the middle part of Ahmici, was the same agreed for the lower part of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Where was the line for Lower Ahmici supposed to be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the right-hand side from my house, above those houses in middle part.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: That is in the middle part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And by the mosque, down there by the mosque since there were a lot of people living there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The road that went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Was that the main road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, no. On the right-hand side, the main part of the road leading to that part of the village, that is to say, on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Can we see this perhaps on the picture? Could we remove this map perhaps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this part of the village (indicating). This slope goes down here, so this is where the line was envisaged, in this part of the village. The planned line was this way, this way and this way (indicating).

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters cannot hear Counsel Slokovic-Glumac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Could you please speak into the microphone?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Could I please walk up to the map so that I could see which part he showed in relation to what he was telling us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this part, in this part of the village and here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: That means above the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. You see the configuration of the terrain here, the slope going down here (indicating)?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: All right. And now in this part of the village? That is the middle part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the middle part. I think that the planned line went this way, this way and this way. I think it went along this road (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: All right. And the upper part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The upper part over here, from one house to another. See? And I think it was envisaged to go somewhere around here. There is a hill here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I wonder if there is a means of putting this on the record. I wonder whether either the Defence counsel or Prosecutor could describe the various defence lines for the record. Could you do so?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes, I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Wonderful.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: So the defence line in Lower Ahmici went behind the lower mosque towards the main road; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I showed it just now, I'll show you again. This part, this part (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: What is the name of that part? There's a forest there too, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's sloped ground here, and that is where the defence line was envisaged (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Well, that is what I said, in the area behind the mosque that goes towards the main road, in that section.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot hear the witness, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: All right. In the middle part of Ahmici where was the defence line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was planned this way, this way and this way (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: So it went over the road that goes to Upper Ahmici and in the area of where the upper mosque was, and it spread from the left and the right-hand side from the road. How far away is that from the road on both sides?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the left and to the right you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly. On the right-hand side perhaps it's about 200 metres, and on the left-hand side more. Perhaps about 300. I don't know, about 300 or 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And Upper Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, below these houses here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Below the houses in Upper Ahmici, along the road that goes to Upper Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Underneath the road and underneath the houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, it would be far more precise if we could draw this on one of these maps, because it would be important for us too, the Defence. So could we perhaps get one from the Prosecutor? So can we have him draw it here so that we would have a copy, or perhaps could we have a photocopy made right now, because I think this would be important for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Are you using P-226? I wonder whether this is big enough. It's only a small part. I don't think it's sufficient. We need a big plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: This would be the best one. It's the same like up there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This photograph is marked D/10.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, could you now draw the lines that I tried to describe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think you will be able to see it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps you could use a different marker or something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, and maybe give numbers to each defence line, 1, 2, 3, 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Could you mark the line and could you put numbers on them, 1, 2, 3, 4?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Marks).

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And what about Lower Ahmici? You can't see it very well over here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's marked too. (Marks).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Could you please use the pointer and now point to the various lines so that we can see on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the line in the lower part of the village. This is the middle part of the village, and this is the line in the upper part of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: In Lower Ahmici you marked the line with 1, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: So could you please do that? And the rest, 2 for the middle part and 3 for the upper part.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Marks).

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please, could you look at the last page of the diary? Just a minute, please. Tell me, the line in the middle part of Ahmici, it goes above the Kupreskic houses, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, where does it go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it's not near the Kupreskics' at all, it's up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: It's above those houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, above those houses and to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me now -- look at this last map that you have in the diary. Is that -- does that approximately correspond to the median line, the middle line that you drew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: When you turn it around; right? Because it's the other way around. Here are the names of the people who are supposed to be at various positions along the line. Was the same kind of sketch made for Upper and Lower Ahmici so that the people who would be in certain sections would be exactly registered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: How many people registered for this lower part of the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As many people as happened to be in the village at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: With weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both with and without weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: These are only names here, and it is about 20 people altogether, and that's why I'm asking you. These are people who were in the village that day, that day that line was made, so they knew they would be in the village. Was it made in such a way for Lower Ahmici too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For all three parts of the village this was planned. That is to say, in case of an attack, the people who happened to be in the village were supposed to go to the line and to defend people, civilians, the old, the young, the feeble, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: So it was the individual names of people that were listed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And how many people were envisaged for Upper Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: More than for the middle part of Ahmici, because there were more people there, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And for Lower Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, like for the middle part of the village. I think that the number is more or less the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: All right. That's more than 60 at any rate. Was the same thing made for Pirici, for this part that you said you also covered with your guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I believe think the same was made for Pirici.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Where did the line go, the line for Pirici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Under, below the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Can we see that there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shall I draw it in?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the large map. You will show it to us on the large map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Marks).

utterances.speaker: MR. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes, number 4.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot hear counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Will you show it on the ELMO, on this machine here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is it. Between the houses. Namely, all the lines were planned to be between the houses, in the house, around the houses, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. This involved a similar number of people, did it the not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there were many -- it was much less in this case. I don't know exactly how many but less.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "in the houses," what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That means that in the event of an attack, people should be there. The moment they ran out of their houses they should be in the right position to defend their houses and their families.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that they would be using their houses as a place from which they would shoot if anything happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, that doesn't mean that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, we have already said this. You were counting, in this exercise, on the people who were in the village because this was done immediately prior to that date, which is to say the 15th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We had such an agreement from before about the establishment of guards, because the moment that Strane, Merdani and the other villages happened and Esad was killed, we were compelled to give some thought to this and to try to find the right solution.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: But on the 15th, in view of the information which you received, you specified this in more detail?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did there exist a storehouse, a depot for weapons in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: How come then that the person who wrote this diary was issued with the weapon from a storehouse because deformulation use was -- "I was issued with armament" -- that was on the 15th of April and he did not take it from somewhere himself, he was issued with arms from a storehouse.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm quite sure that there did not exist a depot of weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: But was there a place where weaponry was kept or some parts of the arsenal, ammunition, for instance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, there was nothing of the kind. The only -- everything which was there was at the frontlines towards the Serbs, the rifles, the ammunition, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Except your rifle. Your rifle was in the village.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And there were more rifles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And there was some ammunition because this man took it on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was ammunition, and how he came by that ammunition, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: It also says here explosives and various charges with plastic explosives and so on. Where did the explosive come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Were the people from the village perhaps --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The people worked at the SPS factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Was it perhaps from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were some people who worked at the SPS factory, but they had not been working for quite some time because it had been occupied so that the Muslims had no access to it at all. They weren't allowed to go up there at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: But in the course of the proceedings, we heard that people did work at the SPS.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did. But at that particular time, in 1992, 1993, they could not access their workplaces at the Slobodan Princip Seljo factory because the HVO had taken it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, how many people were able to go to work because the HVO unit was there? How many people are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nobody could go.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: But were they on hold, were they made redundant, or was work going on at the factory at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. Some of them were on hold, and even those who were supposed to work were not allowed to come and work.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us go back a bit to this part where you refer to the 325th Mountain Brigade. When was it set up? In view of the fact that you took part in its establishment, when was it set up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not organised towards the end. It had not been -- setting up had not been finished at the end of 1993, although we did work on it daily, but we never managed to really organise the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Tell me: How many battalions did it have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Where were the command posts of these?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One was at Kruscica and the other one was at Preocica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And what about Vitez, Stari Vitez? Was there a battalion at Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not a battalion. It was called municipal staff at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: But was there any unit at Stari Vitez which remained there after the attack on Stari Vitez? Not just a staff. You keep referring to a staff. I'm talking about people.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know. Was there a battalion with a command post in the village of Bukve which comprised people from Stara Bila, Sadovace, Bukve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there was no battalion there at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: What was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were these two battalions and the people at Stari Vitez, and what their name was, I think it was the municipal HQ or staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: But when the 325th was formed, there were no more HQs, staffs. Tell me -- so there was a command post of the battalion in Kruscica and the other one at Preocica. Poculica -- what was in Poculica then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing. And was there any unit at Vrhovine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: There was a company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Was there one at Dubravica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Solakovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Sivrino Selo? Another company, the second company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know. What about Pirici, Ahmici, Santici, and Nadioci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: What was there? How many people were there? Was there any sort of an organisation, an organised unit there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: No. So there were only the guards, as you've already said, and individual people who individually were members of the army of the B and H?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was no organised army formation there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: According to which principle were the troops organised? Was it according to the territorial principle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As a rule, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: That means that people from a certain territory would comprise a certain unit, make up a certain unit; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I say usually, yes, although it was not that way in all cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Was it according to the territorial principle that the 325th was set up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And these individual battalions which comprised the population from the territory of the municipality of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the 325th Brigade was from Vitez, so it was only natural that people from that particular region would be used to man it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: So it depended on the size and the number of people in a certain area, but the people in a certain area would also be organised into certain units depending on the size?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I'm saying that people from a certain area, from certain villages or places, were organised into units according to the territorial principle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: That means that people who lived in the area of Ahmici, Santici, and Pirici also had this kind of organisation, according to the territorial principle; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All of these people belonged to 325th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: To lower formations, you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. But which people belonged to which formations, that I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: All right. In relation to this part that -- oh, just a minute, please. So in relation to Ahmici, what was the place that you were at? This diary speaks of the command, so I am going to simplify matters to: Where was the command in Ahmici? Where did you usually meet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was not a specified place.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Was it the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Where was the radio station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The radio station was in the house of Nasid Ahmic, the old house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: That is not the house of the Nasid Ahmic that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this is his new house. He had an old house up there in the other part of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Was that house abandoned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Who manned the radio station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Several people worked there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Was duty organised round the clock at the radio station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes, yes; sometimes, no. It all depended on the man who was on duty. It depended on his conscience, whether he would be there all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: However, what was envisaged? Full-time duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know when this duty started at the radio station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I couldn't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: At the time when you were in the village and when you were dealing with this organisation, who was the radio operator? Who do you know as the radio operator?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that Husein Ahmic worked there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: What radio station was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: RUP 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Was this radio station transferred on the 16th; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Who were they linked to through this radio station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With the command of the battalion in Preocica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Was there also communication with some other places?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall. I'm not sure. I think there was, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I have it written down somewhere and I can remind you of it, but obviously I can't find it. Was there communication with Kruscica, Vraniska, Vrhovine, Poculica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And with some of these places?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think so. I don't think there was any communication with these places.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I would now have to put a direct question involving a name too, so could we please move into a closed session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, we will move into a closed session. (Closed session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: 5.00 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 30th day of September, 1998, at 9.00 a.m.
